notes.children: A `children` map's entries are EITHER a bare childTaskId string (childIndex = its array position) OR an explicit { childTaskId, childIndex } object. The object form exists to put childIndex DELIBERATELY out of array order, which is the only way to observe that both applyMemberRules and planDerivedTasks sort children by childIndex before using them.
notes.sourceWindows: `sourceWindows` values are bare timeframe strings; the harness wraps each into a BoardWindow with startDate = null and endDate = null before passing it as `sourceWindowByTaskId`. Swift must wrap identically or CUSTOM handling will diverge.
notes.windowDates: Board windows in the planDerivedTasks / derivedRows sections carry the OFFSET-LESS LOCAL ISO shape production writes (wizardLocalISOString / toLocalISO), e.g. 2026-09-18T00:00:00 - never a date-only 2026-09-18. computeWindowBaseline documents date-only as unsupported (JS parses it as UTC midnight; the Swift ISO parser has no date-only format at all), and refreshDerivedBaselines feeds a stored row's own startDate straight back in as a boundary, so these vectors must not normalise the one shape that would make the two platforms disagree. The CUSTOM windowDays vectors are the deliberate exception - dayNumber is date-only by contract there.
notes.sourceWindowByTaskId: Keyed by every id whose source window matters - supplied members AND the children of a One-square compound. A compound's parts are pro-rated by looking up the CHILD's id (e.g. c1), never the compound's (C), so sourceWindows deliberately carries NO entry for C or C2: an implementation that keys the lookup by the compound id gets null source days, skips pro-rating and fails the One-square auto vectors.
notes.frozenDerivedRow: isFrozenDerivedRow(task, now): a window-stamped derived row (isWindowStampedDerived: sharedCounterId + startDate + createdInWizard) whose endDate is STRICTLY before now is skipped by shared-counter increment/decrement/undo propagation. endDate is inclusive (isWithinTimeframe convention). A JSON null startDate/endDate means the field is absent. Instants are Z-suffixed so the vectors are time-zone independent.
notes.frozenRowReachedByEvent: isFrozenRowReachedByEvent(task, occurredAt, now): undo across the window end. True iff the row is frozen at now (isFrozenDerivedRow) AND occurredAt lies inside the row's own [startDate, endDate] (isWithinTimeframe, inclusive both ends). Undo then cascades (never writes) that row's boards. Z-suffixed instants.

varyRange.name: half-up tie: t=5 lvl2 then [round(2.5)=3, round(7.5)=8]

Before this rule c4 placed as-is (no startDate, vary off). Vary off takes no sample; n1 (normal) is still placed as-is. two rolls consume rng in selectedIds order: r1 (board auto 5, lvl1 [4,6]) then r2 (pool lvl1 [8,12])

vectors.name: third sample never taken: three level-1 rolls r1 [4,6], r2 [8,12], c1 (board auto 2 then [2,2] lo==hi so NO sample)

vectors.name: split part with a target on a pool source then placed as-is
vectors.note: The part-level twin of the member-level pool vector: target 5 is ignored because the source is a pool, and with no vary there is nothing left to derive, so c1 is placed as its original self. Contrast the board-source split vector, where the same part target yields a derived counter.

vectors.name: children roll in childIndex order, not array order
vectors.note: C2's children are stored [c1 (childIndex 1), c3 (childIndex 0)], so childIndex order is c3 then c1 - the reverse of array order. c3 (childIndex 0) first: target 10 vary 1, goal 20, varyRange(10,1,20) = [max(1,round(8))=8, min(20,round(12)=12)=12] = [8,12]; sample1 = 1083814273/2^32 = 0.25235, 8 + floor(0.25235 x 5 = 1.2617) = 9. c1 (childIndex 1) second: target 6 vary 2, goal 8, varyRange(6,2,8) = [max(1,round(3))=3, round(9)=9] = [3,9] (hi overshoots the goal 8 - no ceiling since 2026-10-06); sample2 = 378494188/2^32 = 0.08813, 3 + floor(0.08813 x 7 = 0.6169) = 3. Array order would instead give c1 = 3+floor(0.25235x7=1.766) = 4 and c3 = 8+floor(0.08813x5=0.441) = 8, so this vector discriminates. Both parts derive, so expectedRngCalls is 2.

vectors.name: One-square compound with a part target on a pool source then as-is
vectors.note: The One-square twin of the split-part pool vector, and the pool counterpart of the board vector directly above: a part-level target is ignored on a pool source, so no part derives, the whole compound is placed as its original self, and the rng is untouched. This is also the only vector that reaches the "a rule exists but derives nothing" exit (as opposed to the no-rule-at-all exit).

vectors.name: action-less counting member keeps its own title
vectors.note: a1 has no action and no unit, so the derived draft carries action = "" and unit = "" and the title falls back to the source task's own title rather than a generated "<action> <n> <unit>" string. Target is autoTarget(12,7,1) = min(12, ceil(12/7) = 2) = 2, vary 0 so the rng is untouched.

vectors.name: two parts of one compound sharing a counter root collapse to ONE child and take NO extra sample
vectors.note: C3's children are r2 (childIndex 0, its own root) and c4 (childIndex 1, sharedCounterId r2) - the same counter family authored twice inside one compound, which counter-family exclusivity does NOT prevent (it constrains board selection, not compound authorship). r2: goal 10, monthly source to a daily board, autoTarget = min(10, ceil(10 x 1 / 30) = 1) = 1; varyRange(1, 1, 10) = [max(1, round(0.8)) = 1, min(10, round(1.2)) = 1] = [1,1], so lo == hi and the roll takes no sample. c4: goal 4, root r2, so the per-root dedupe hits BEFORE the roll and c4 takes no sample either - hence expectedRngCalls 0. Both parts resolve to the SAME derived id, so the children list collapses to one entry (first in childIndex order, keeping childIndex 0); without the collapse the compound would carry one childTaskId - and one linkId, a pure function of (compound, child) - twice.

vectors.name: the per-root dedupe is checked BEFORE the roll: a collapsed part consumes no sample
vectors.note: The discriminating twin of the vector above. There c4's own range was degenerate ([1,1]) so the sample count could not tell roll-then-dedupe from dedupe-then-roll. Here c4 carries an explicit part target 5, clamped to its goal 4, and varyRange(4, 1, 4) = [max(1, round(3.2)) = 3, round(4.8) = 5] = [3,5] - a NON-degenerate range that would consume a sample if the roll ran. It must not: c4's root is r2, which r2 (childIndex 0) already minted, so the dedupe returns that draft before rolling and expectedRngCalls stays 0. Roll-before-dedupe would make it 1 and leave the seeded sequence dependent on how many members happen to collapse. r2 itself is unchanged (auto target 1, [1,1], no sample), and the collapsed children list is the same single entry.

vectors.name: no identical clone: d1 pulled daily to daily so the auto target is its own goal 12, vary off then the ROOT d1 is placed and NOTHING is minted
vectors.note: Owner ruling 2026-09-22. Every OTHER board vector pulls cross-timeframe, so it pro-rates and still derives; d1 is the same-timeframe case, where autoTarget(12, 1, 1) returns the goal unchanged and the derived row would be a byte-for-byte clone of its root (same target, same regenerated title) - the 'Read 1 book' twin the owner saw on device. The literal root id 'd1' must land in placement and derived must be EMPTY. expectedRngCalls 0 also pins that the skip is decided before any roll, so a seeded sequence cannot shift.

vectors.name: vary rescues the same-timeframe pull: d1 target==goal 12 but lvl1 then [10,14]; seed 42 gives 10+floor(0.2523x5=1.26)=11; d1's CUSTOM title 'Push-ups 12' is kept on the rolled copy
vectors.note: The skip needs BOTH halves - target == goal AND vary off. A vary range is a real difference from the root, so the identical-looking pull still mints, and the rolled 11 (not 12) proves the derived row is not a clone. Title flipped 2026-10-06 (custom-counter-title fix): d1's stored title 'Push-ups 12' is NOT the auto title for Push-ups / 12 / reps ('Push-ups 12 reps'), so it is a custom name and counterCopyTitle carries it over verbatim - the copy is titled 'Push-ups 12' at target 11, never 'Push-ups 11 reps' as before the fix.

vectors.name: no identical clone via an explicit rule: r1 target 35 equals its own goal 35, vary off then the ROOT r1 is placed
vectors.note: The skip reads resolveTarget's RESULT, not how it got there: a hand-set target that happens to equal the goal collapses exactly like the same-timeframe auto target, even though r1 is pulled weekly to daily and would otherwise pro-rate to 5 (see the first vector in this section). This is the discriminating pair for a naive implementation that only checks 'is the source window the same'.

vectors.name: no identical clone on a split part: board source, parts.c1.target 8 equals c1's own goal 8, vary off then the ROOT part c1 is placed
vectors.note: The part-branch twin of the member vectors. Contrast 'split part on a board source ... part target 3 overrides to 3', which is the same shape with target 3 != goal 8 and DOES mint. c2 (a normal task) is placed as itself in both.

vectors.name: the skip requires the member to BE a root: w1 is already a window-stamped derived counter, so a same-timeframe board pull with vary off STILL MINTS rather than placing another window's row
vectors.note: The wrong-window guard. w1 carries sharedCounterId r1 AND startDate 2026-09-17 - it is yesterday's daily row, and resolveBoardSourceSupply happily lets it into today's supply. autoTarget(5, 1, 1) returns the goal 5 unchanged, so target == goal and vary is off: without the `sharedCounterId == null` half of the condition this would place w1 itself, putting YESTERDAY's window-stamped row on today's board (its startDate still names the old window, so the derived-counter carve-out reads the old baseline and the square can open already complete, and refreshDerivedBaselines recomputes from the same stale startDate so it never heals). It must re-mint for THIS window instead - collapsing onto root r1, which is why the placement is derived:r1 and the draft replaces w1 while sourcing from it. Baseline 12 is r1 own, freshly taken for this window. The hand-added branch has always guarded this with isWindowStampedMember.

vectors.name: custom title survives the mint: hand-added LINKED member h1 (root r1, goal 6, title 'Morning pages' != auto 'Read 6 pages') is minted for this window and the copy keeps 'Morning pages' verbatim
vectors.note: Owner bug 2026-10-06: a counting task given a custom name in the wizard showed its default '{Action} {goal} {unit}' name once the board was created, because the mint regenerated the copy's title whenever action was set. The rule now: a title is custom iff non-empty after trimming AND different (case-sensitive, trimmed) from generateCounterTaskTitle(own action, own maxCount, own unit); a custom title carries over verbatim. h1 is the owner's exact shape - a wizard-created counter auto-linked to hub root r1 (sharedCounterId set, no startDate), hand-added, vary off, always minted since 2026-10-01.

vectors.name: auto title is regenerated at the copy's target: hand-added LINKED member c4 (title 'Run 4 miles' == auto) with manualTaskVary lvl1 then [3,4]; seed 42 gives 3 and the copy is titled 'Run 3 miles'
vectors.note: The control for the custom-title vector: c4's title IS its auto title, so the copy's title follows the copy's NEW maxCount exactly as before the 2026-10-06 fix. varyRange(4, 1, 4) = [max(1, round(3.2)) = 3, round(4.8) = 5] = [3,5]; sample1 = 0.25235 so 3 + floor(0.25235 x 3 = 0.757) = 3.

vectors.name: custom title survives pro-rating (and a whole-kind mint floors the fractional baseline 1.2 to 1): board-sourced r3 (goal 35, title 'Big read' != auto 'Read 35 pages') weekly to daily gives target 5 and the copy keeps 'Big read'
vectors.note: Same shape as the first vector in this section (r1 35 weekly to daily gives autoTarget ceil(35/7) = 5) but with a custom name: the user chose 'Big read', so the pro-rated copy is still 'Big read', not 'Read 5 pages'. Baseline 0 (r3 has no events).

vectors.name: CONTINUOUS board member: k1 (26.2 miles) monthly to a WEEKLY board then one draft maxCount 6.2, countKind continuous, title 'Run 6.2 miles'
vectors.note: A vector may carry its own `window`, overriding the section's daily one (the harness then checks the drafts against it). autoTarget pro-rates in 0.1 steps: ceil(26.2x7/30 = 6.113) = 6.2.

vectors.name: CONTINUOUS board member with vary a little: target 6.2, range [round(4.96)=5, round(7.44)=7.4] = 25 tenths, seed 42 then 5 + floor(0.2523x25)x0.1 = 5.6 - exactly one rng sample
DURATION board member rides the whole branch: m1 (600 minutes) monthly to a WEEKLY board then 600x7/30 = 140, countKind duration
R17 off-step continuous goal on a SAME-length board: k2 (26.25) weekly to weekly, dice off then the target is the goal 26.25 itself, so NO clone is minted - k2 is placed as the root
R17 continuous goal below the step: k3 (0.05) monthly to weekly auto-targets min(0.05, ceil-to-0.1(0.0117)) = 0.05 = the goal, so k3 is placed as the root, never re-stepped to 0.1

planDerivedTasks.idPinsNote: Literal uuidv5 outputs, computed ONCE with the TS uuidv5 (default OYBC namespace). Swift must reproduce them independently. Names: 'sources:derived:<boardId>:<root>', 'sources:derived-compound:<boardId>:<compound>', 'sources:derived-link:<derivedCompoundId>:<childId>'. The link name's <childId> is the LITERAL child task id - a derived uuid for a derived child, the raw source id for an original one. idPins itself is a clean token -> uuid map with no stray keys.

windowBaseline.name: sums live increments strictly before the boundary
windowBaseline.note: 5+7 = 12; the 9 is AT the boundary (the comparison is strictly <, not <=), and the tombstoned 100, the other root's 50 and both completion events are ignored. The second completion carries a delta - a shape the schema forbids, but the kind filter must reject it on its own rather than leaning on the missing-delta guard, or a malformed remote row would inflate the baseline by 40. The last row is the other malformed shape: an increment with NO delta, which must be skipped rather than summed - adding `undefined` would turn the whole baseline into NaN, and max(0, NaN) is NaN, which would then be written onto the derived row.

windowBaseline.name: negative sum clamps to 0
windowBaseline.note: A decrement-only history sums to -3; the baseline is a count, so it clamps at 0 (max(0, sum)).

windowBaseline.name: an event half an hour before the boundary counts
windowBaseline.note: Both stamps are offset-bearing, so this vector means the same thing in every timezone. The instants-not-strings invariant is pinned by the mixed-form vector below, not here.

windowBaseline.name: mixed forms compare as instants, not as strings
windowBaseline.note: 00:30+02:00 is 2026-09-17T22:30Z - BEFORE the boundary instant - so it counts. A lexical compare sees "2026-09-18T00:30" > "2026-09-18T00:00" and drops it, so this vector fails on any string comparison, in every timezone.

windowBaseline.name: an unparseable occurredAt skips that event only
windowBaseline.note: RB2: a failed parse on either side skips the event rather than counting it - an unparseable stamp must never silently inflate a window baseline.

windowBaseline.name: an unparseable boundary skips every event
windowBaseline.note: The other half of the same rule: with no usable boundary nothing can be shown to precede it, so the baseline is 0.

derivedRows.note: buildDerivedRows turns the planDerivedTasks drafts into full Task / CompoundChild rows. Ids are TOKENS resolved through `ids` below. Unlike the planDerivedTasks section (whose short r1/c1 names are only ever map keys), these ids are uuid-shaped because the produced rows are asserted against Zod TaskSchema / CompoundChildSchema, which require a uuid for id, sharedCounterId, compoundTaskId and childTaskId - that schema pass is the completeness check that no required Task field was forgotten. The derived / link ids in `ids` are literal uuidv5 outputs of derivedTaskId / derivedCompoundId / derivedLinkId over `boardId` plus those uuids, pinned by their own test. Expected `tasks` / `links` are SUBSET matches (every listed field is asserted; unlisted fields are not), but the ORDER and LENGTH of both arrays are asserted in full: derived counters in draft order first, then derived compounds. An `expectedAbsent` list on an expected row asserts those fields are absent/undefined on the produced row - it is how the null-threshold rule is pinned (a draft threshold of null must produce NO threshold field, because Zod rejects an explicit null there).
derivedRows.idsNote: R1 / R2 are shared-counter roots, K1 / K2 the two children of the source compound C (K1 counting, K2 not), all keyed by token. `roots` and `compounds` are keyed by the same tokens and resolved to their uuids before the call.

vectors.name: a continuous draft writes its countKind and its fractional goal (12-12=0 < 6.2)
vectors.note: The draft's countKind is copied onto the Task row verbatim; absent on a draft reads as discrete.

vectors.name: one derived counter: mirror + isCompleted false (12-12=0 < 5)
vectors.note: currentCount MIRRORS the root's lifetime count (12) rather than the window count; the window value is derived from it and `baseline` at read time, so displayed = max(0, 12-12) = 0, which is below the target 5.

vectors.name: isCompleted latches true at mint when mirror minus baseline is at or above the target (3-0=3 >= 2)
vectors.note: A fresh window whose root has already accumulated past the target is born complete - the mint runs the same deriveDisplayedCount the read path does, so it must not be hand-initialised to false. `completedAt` is stamped at the same moment: the false-to-true transition every other write path stamps it on has already happened here, so a row left without it would never get one.

vectors.name: derived compound: parent row + two links, derived child first
vectors.note: The compound row copies title / operator from the draft and `description` from the SOURCE compound (compounds map), carries the same window as its parts, and is born isCompleted false (a compound row's isCompleted is written for column uniformity and never read). Its null threshold must not be written as null - see expectedAbsent.

vectors.name: M_OF_N compound carries its operator and threshold through
vectors.note: The positive half of the threshold rule: a real threshold IS written (the vector above pins that a null one is not). Same drafts as the vector above apart from operator / threshold.

vectors.name: an action-less draft writes no action / unit rather than empty strings
vectors.note: planDerivedTasks fills action / unit with "" for a counter that has neither (the title then falls back to the source task's own). Empty strings must not reach the row: the column stays absent, exactly as a hand-made action-less counter would be. Displayed = max(0, 3-3) = 0 < 2, so it is not complete.

notes.seededTargets: seededTargetsForSource vectors reuse the bare-timeframe window convention above (a missing `sourceWindow` key means the field is OMITTED, i.e. the span is unknowable). `tasks` carries only the two fields the calculation reads - `type` and an optional `maxCount` - matching TS's Pick<Task,'type'|'maxCount'> and Swift's BoardSources.SeededTargetTask. Every `expected` value is hand-computed as autoTarget(max(1, goal - windowCount), sourceDays, targetDays), never read back from the function under test.
notes.windows: effectiveMemberTarget's and prefilledOneOffTarget's sourceWindow / targetWindow vectors use bare timeframe strings, wrapped by the harness into a BoardWindow with startDate = null and endDate = null - same convention as planDerivedTasks.sourceWindows above. A vector with no `sourceWindow` key means the field is omitted (undefined), not null. A CUSTOM window needs real bounds, so prefilledOneOffTarget vectors may carry `sourceWindowDates` / `targetWindowDates` as a [start, end] array of YYYY-MM-DD strings; a one-element array means the end bound is MISSING (the harness passes null for it), which is how the unknowable-span branch is pinned.
notes.fromBoard: effectiveMemberTarget's `fromBoard` mirrors planDerivedTasks' resolveTarget gate exactly, and since the owner ruling of 2026-09-21 that gate is `fromBoard` ALONE: auto-targeting (the autoTarget call) runs for any board-sourced member, one-off and recurring alike, so the vectors below deliberately carry BOTH modes with otherwise identical inputs and the same expected number. A pool-sourced or hand-added member (`fromBoard: false`) still always falls to `explicit ?? goal`, even with a known sourceWindow - that surviving half of the gate is why the two 'pool-sourced' vectors below carry a `sourceWindow` that is never actually read. `mode` is still passed (and still on the TS/Swift signatures) but is no longer read by either helper.
notes.keepVaryOff: A withMemberRule step may carry `keepVaryOff: true` (absent = false): the harness passes it as withMemberRule's options (`{ keepVaryOff }` on TS, the `keepVaryOff:` argument on Swift). With it a merged `vary: 0` is STORED as an explicit per-board off (pool-level defaults, 2026-10-06) instead of being pruned; every other pruning rule is unchanged. withPartRule steps never carry it.
notes.patchShape: withMemberRule / withPartRule vectors write a patch as `{ "set": { field: value, ... }, "clear": [ field, ... ] }` - either key may be absent (an empty step patches nothing). `set` overwrites a field to the given value (including a default like `vary: 0` or `split: false` - a deliberate explicit set, still pruned by the same default-pruning rule as any other route to that value); `clear` deletes a field entirely, the same as passing `undefined` to the TS API. The harness builds the actual TS patch object as `{ ...set, ...Object.fromEntries(clear.map(k => [k, undefined])) }` before calling withMemberRule/withPartRule, so the TS function signature itself is untouched (`Partial<Rule>`, `undefined` still deletes). `steps` applies withMemberRule/withPartRule in order to the SAME source, threading each result into the next call - this is how the 'set then clear' vectors are two real calls, not one. `expectedMemberRules: null` asserts the result has NO `memberRules` key at all (`'memberRules' in result === false`), not that the key is present with value null.
notes.swiftPatchDecoding: The `set` / `clear` split exists specifically so a Swift decoder can tell 'field absent from the patch, leave alone' from 'field explicitly cleared' without relying on JSON `null`, which a synthesized `Decodable` cannot distinguish from a missing key via `decodeIfPresent`. Swift's per-field patch type should decode to a three-state `enum { case keep, clear, set(Value) }` per field: a field present in `set` decodes to `.set(value)`, a field present (by name) in `clear` decodes to `.clear`, and a field in neither decodes to `.keep` - never infer `.clear` from an absent key. This keeps the Swift twin's decode step a direct mirror of the harness's `{ ...set, ...clear-as-undefined }` merge, rather than requiring `container.contains(forKey:)` probing against a single ambiguous object.
notes.varyRangeLabelNull: varyRangeLabel's level-0 vectors carry `"expected": null`; unlike the patch case above there is no 'leave alone vs. clear' ambiguity here - a Swift `expected: String?` field decodes JSON `null` the same way standard synthesized `Decodable` already handles it, so no sentinel or extra note is needed beyond this one.

notes.model: Pool-level default dice (docs/BOARD_SOURCES.md §Member rules → Pool-level defaults, 2026-10-06). `Pool.memberVary` is task id → VaryLevel; only 1 | 2 are ever STORED (prunePoolMemberVary drops a 0, the same default-pruning rule withMemberRule applies to a source rule). Pool defaults are LIVE — pulling a pool stores NO rule on the source; effectiveMemberRules is the read-time FALLBACK every reader applies (persist / spawn / Preview / the member row): a stored source `vary` always wins, the pool default fills in only where the member's stored rule carries no `vary` at all. Nothing here is persisted — the effective map is handed to the planner in place of the stored row.
notes.shapes: `pool` carries only the three fields the helpers read — `id`, `taskIds`, and an optional `memberVary` map (a MISSING key means the field is absent, which both platforms read as an empty map). `source` carries `sourceId`, `kind` and an optional `memberRules` (null = no key, exactly as the display vectors above). The harness wraps each into a full BoardSource / Pool with neutral values for every other field. `memberVary` values are raw ints so Swift maps them through VaryLevel(rawValue:).
notes.shouldKeepVaryOff: shouldKeepVaryOff vectors use the same `pool` shape (null = no pool); `expected` is the bare boolean a Sources-sheet setter passes as withMemberRule's keepVaryOff.
notes.unchangedSource: effectiveMemberRules vectors carry `unchangedSource`: true pins that withEffectiveMemberRules returns its input UNCHANGED — the identical object on TS (`toBe`), an equal value on Swift — so a source that inherits nothing stays byte-identical (a rule-less source keeps NO memberRules key, never gains `{}`). false pins that the returned copy's memberRules equal `expected`. `expected` is always the full effective map as effectiveMemberRules returns it, `{}` when empty.
